hook: Water bath canning: the real basics
hook_sub: What that big pot is for

slides.t: A deep pot with a rack. Filled jars sit under boiling water, which drives out air and seals the lids.
Fruit, jams, pickles and tomatoes with added acid. Plain vegetables, beans and meat need a pressure canner.
Jars sit on the rack under at least 1 inch of water. Start the timer only once it reaches a full rolling boil.
A pot deep enough for jars plus water, a rack, a jar lifter and a funnel. A flat bottom suits most stoves.
Guessing recipes, reusing lids, skipping altitude time. Use tested recipes and let jars cool 12 to 24 hours.

hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything

slides.t: Bypass blades slide past each other like scissors for clean cuts on live stems. Anvil types crush, so suit dead wood.
Stems and branches up to about 3/4 inch. Thicker wood calls for loppers or a pruning saw.
A grip that fits their hand, a lock that is easy to work, and a blade that can be sharpened.
Cut just above a bud at a slight angle, with the sharp blade on the side of the plant that stays.
Wipe off sap after use, oil the pivot now and then, and clean the blades between sick plants.
